argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrow, caveated defense of certification. Aggregate readiness passes by 2.2 points and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports launch readiness at the overall system level. The same record also shows a current veterans benefits intake regression below the warning threshold, that prior approval is stale for this retrieval configuration and eval batch, and that the release-thread monitoring note is not approved mitigation or disclosure. On this record, the strongest supportable position is not clean compliance; it is that certification can be treated as caveated only if the audit packet is understood as explicitly carrying forward the current evaluation results and the veterans-benefits limitation as a material disclosed limitation for this launch.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim about business cost is needed to resolve the audit question on the admissible record.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not allow prior approval or informal monitoring to substitute for current release documentation, approved mitigation, or approved risk acceptance. Public governance guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring risk is directionally supportive, but it does not replace the policy predicate. Accordingly, the supportable interpretation is that aggregate readiness and rehearsal results justify a narrowed certification posture only with an explicit caveat tied to the current documented subgroup weakness, not an unconditional finding of present compliance on the existing record.
concessions: The current admissible record does not prove that the required disclosure text is already present in current release documentation.
The veterans benefits intake slice is a current material weakness for a named launch use case.
The prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration and eval batch, so it cannot independently satisfy current-release requirements.
The release-thread monitoring comment is not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language.
